```{r}
library("randomForest")
library("caret")
library("tidyverse")
library("here")
```

## Set up 

```{r}
# Loading the dataset
analysis_tpm <- readRDS(here("data", "processed", "analysis_tpm.rds"))

# visualizing dataset
analysis_tpm[, 1:10] %>%
  head(5)

# removing unexpressed genes
gene_columns <- 8:ncol(analysis_tpm)

analysis_tpm <- analysis_tpm %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(gene_columns), as.numeric))

gene_totals <- colSums(analysis_tpm[, gene_columns],
                       na.rm = TRUE)

expressed_genes <- names(gene_totals[gene_totals > 0])
```

```{r}
# Outcome
Y <- analysis_tpm$pf_d7

X_genes <- as.matrix(analysis_tpm[, expressed_genes, drop = FALSE])
```

Running rf at this stage failed due to the huge number of genes. 
Let's select the top 500 most variable genes within training folds as an exploratory starting point. 

```{r}
select_top_genes <- function(X, n_genes = 500) {

  gene_variance <- apply(X, 2, var)

  gene_variance <- gene_variance[
    is.finite(gene_variance) & gene_variance > 0
  ]

  selected_genes <- names(
    sort(gene_variance, decreasing = TRUE)
  )[seq_len(min(n_genes, length(gene_variance)))]

  selected_genes
}

## tuning parameters 
rf_grid <- c(5, 15, 30)
```

# Random forest LOOCV on the orignal scale

Outer LOOCV: holds out one participant to evaluate prediction
Inner LOOCV: tunes mtry using only the 28 outer-training participants

```{r}
# Store predictions
rf_predictions <- rep(NA_real_, length(Y))

# Store baseline predictions
rf_baseline_predictions <- rep(NA_real_, length(Y))

# Store best mtry
rf_best_mtry <- rep(NA_integer_, length(Y))

# Store variable importance
rf_importance <- vector("list", length(Y))

set.seed(123)

# OUTER LOOCV
for (i in seq_along(Y)) {

  cat("Outer LOOCV:", i, "of", length(Y), "\n")

  # Hold out one participant
  X_train <- X_genes[-i, , drop = FALSE]
  X_test <- X_genes[i, , drop = FALSE]

  y_train <- Y[-i]

  # Store inner CV RMSE
  inner_rmse <- rep(NA_real_, length(rf_grid))

  # INNER LOOCV: tune mtry
  for (j in seq_along(rf_grid)) {

    inner_predictions <- rep(NA_real_, length(y_train))

    for (k in seq_along(y_train)) {

      # Hold out one participant from outer training set
      X_inner_train <- X_train[-k, , drop = FALSE]
      X_inner_val <- X_train[k, , drop = FALSE]

      y_inner_train <- y_train[-k]

      # Select genes using inner training participants only
      selected_genes <- select_top_genes(
        X_inner_train,
        n_genes = 500
      )

      X_inner_train_selected <- X_inner_train[
        , selected_genes, drop = FALSE
      ]

      X_inner_val_selected <- X_inner_val[
        , selected_genes, drop = FALSE
      ]

      # Fit Random Forest
      rf_model <- randomForest(
        x = X_inner_train_selected,
        y = y_inner_train,
        ntree = 500,
        mtry = min(rf_grid[j], length(selected_genes))
      )

      # Predict held-out inner participant
      inner_predictions[k] <- predict(
        rf_model,
        newdata = X_inner_val_selected
      )
    }

    # Inner LOOCV RMSE
    inner_rmse[j] <- sqrt(
      mean((y_train - inner_predictions)^2)
    )
  }

  # Select best mtry
  best_mtry <- rf_grid[which.min(inner_rmse)]

  rf_best_mtry[i] <- best_mtry

  # Select genes using all 28 outer training participants
  selected_genes <- select_top_genes(
    X_train,
    n_genes = 500
  )

  X_train_selected <- X_train[
    , selected_genes, drop = FALSE
  ]

  X_test_selected <- X_test[
    , selected_genes, drop = FALSE
  ]

  # Fit final outer model
  rf_final <- randomForest(
    x = X_train_selected,
    y = y_train,
    ntree = 1000,
    mtry = min(best_mtry, length(selected_genes)),
    importance = TRUE
  )

  # Predict held-out participant
  rf_predictions[i] <- predict(
    rf_final,
    newdata = X_test_selected
  )

  # Baseline prediction
  rf_baseline_predictions[i] <- mean(y_train)

  # Store variable importance
  imp <- importance(rf_final, type = 1)

  rf_importance[[i]] <- data.frame(
    gene = rownames(imp),
    importance = as.numeric(imp[, 1])
  )
}
```
## Performance calculation

```{r}
# Random Forest
rf_rmse <- sqrt(
  mean((Y - rf_predictions)^2)
)

rf_r2 <- 1 -
  sum((Y - rf_predictions)^2) /
  sum((Y - mean(Y))^2)

# Baseline
rf_baseline_rmse <- sqrt(
  mean((Y - rf_baseline_predictions)^2)
)

rf_baseline_r2 <- 1 -
  sum((Y - rf_baseline_predictions)^2) /
  sum((Y - mean(Y))^2)

# Compare
data.frame(
  Model = c("Random Forest", "Baseline"),
  RMSE = c(rf_rmse, rf_baseline_rmse),
  R_squared = c(rf_r2, rf_baseline_r2)
)

## tunning results
data.frame(
  Participant = seq_along(Y),
  Best_mtry = rf_best_mtry
)
```
Compared with the baseline RMSE of 0.0079, Random Forest has improved predictive accuracy.

# Re-running RF LOOCV on the log transformed 

```{r} 
# Log-transform Day 7 plasmablast frequency
y_log <- log(Y)

summary(y_log)
```

## Performance calculation on the original scale

```{r}
# Back-transform Random Forest predictions
log_rf_predictions_original <- exp(log_rf_predictions)

# Back-transform baseline predictions
log_rf_baseline_predictions_original <- exp(
  log_rf_baseline_predictions
)
```

##  Model compoarison
```{r}
# Create comparison table

model_comparison <- data.frame(

  Model = c(
    "Original Random Forest",
    "Original Baseline",
    "Log Random Forest (log scale)",
    "Log Baseline (log scale)",
    "Log Random Forest (original scale)",
    "Log Baseline (original scale)"
  ),

  RMSE = c(

    # Original Random Forest
    rf_rmse,

    # Original baseline
    rf_baseline_rmse,

    # Log Random Forest: log scale
    log_rf_rmse,

    # Log baseline: log scale
    log_rf_baseline_rmse,

    # Log Random Forest: back-transformed
    sqrt(mean((Y - log_rf_predictions_original)^2)),

    # Log baseline: back-transformed
    sqrt(mean((Y - log_rf_baseline_predictions_original)^2))
  ),

  R_squared = c(

    # Original Random Forest
    rf_r2,

    # Original baseline
    rf_baseline_r2,

    # Log Random Forest: log scale
    log_rf_r2,

    # Log baseline: log scale
    log_rf_baseline_r2,

    # Log Random Forest: back-transformed
    1 - sum((Y - log_rf_predictions_original)^2) /
      sum((Y - mean(Y))^2),

    # Log baseline: back-transformed
    1 - sum((Y - log_rf_baseline_predictions_original)^2) /
      sum((Y - mean(Y))^2)
  )
)

# Display results
model_comparison

write.csv(
  model_comparison,
  here("output", "rf_model_comparison.csv"),
  row.names = TRUE
)
```
 This suggests that the log transformation did not improve the predictive performance of your Random Forest due to lower RMSE at the original scale.
 
 Further analysis will however use the log transform outcome due to the skewness of the original data
 
## Additional analysis
```{r}
# Extract additional predictors
clinical_data <- data.frame(
  age = analysis_tpm$age,
  sex = factor(analysis_tpm$biological_sex),
  vaccination = analysis_tpm$n_prior_vax
)
```

For vaccination history, data is missing for two participants. They currentyl have analysis_tpm$n_prior_vax = 0. Performing median imputation rather than removing them. 

```{r}
impute_median <- function(train, test, variable) {

median_value <- median(
    train[[variable]][train[[variable]] != 0],
    na.rm = TRUE
  )

  train[[variable]][train[[variable]] == 0] <- median_value
  test[[variable]][test[[variable]] == 0] <- median_value

  list(train = train, test = test)
}
```

```{r}
run_nested_rf <- function(clinical_vars = character(0)) {

# Store predictions
predictions <- rep(NA_real_, length(y_log))

# Store baseline predictions
baseline_predictions <- rep(NA_real_, length(y_log))

# Store best mtry
best_mtry <- rep(NA_integer_, length(y_log))

# Store variable importance
rf_importance <- vector("list", length(y_log))

set.seed(123)

# OUTER LOOCV
for (i in seq_along(y_log)) {

  cat("Outer LOOCV:", i, "of", length(y_log), "\n")

  # Hold out one participant
  X_train <- X_genes[-i, , drop = FALSE]
  X_test <- X_genes[i, , drop = FALSE]

  y_train <- y_log[-i]

# Split clinical variables
  clinical_train <- clinical_data[-i, , drop = FALSE]
  clinical_test <- clinical_data[i, , drop = FALSE]
  
# Impute missing vaccination history using the outer training median
if ("vaccination" %in% clinical_vars) {

  imputed <- impute_median(
    clinical_train,
    clinical_test,
    "vaccination"
  )

  clinical_train <- imputed$train
  clinical_test <- imputed$test
}

# Store inner CV RMSE
  inner_rmse <- rep(NA_real_, length(rf_grid))

# INNER LOOCV: tune mtry
for (j in seq_along(rf_grid)) {

  inner_predictions <- rep(NA_real_, length(y_train))

    for (k in seq_along(y_train)) {

    # Hold out one participant from outer training set
      X_inner_train <- X_train[-k, , drop = FALSE]
      X_inner_val <- X_train[k, , drop = FALSE]

      y_inner_train <- y_train[-k]

      # Split inner clinical data
      clinical_inner_train <- clinical_train[
          -k, , drop = FALSE]

      clinical_inner_val <- clinical_train[
          k, , drop = FALSE ]
      
      # Impute missing vaccination history 
      if ("vaccination" %in% clinical_vars) {

        imputed <- impute_median(
           clinical_inner_train,
           clinical_inner_val, 
           "vaccination"
        )

        clinical_inner_train <- imputed$train
        clinical_inner_val <- imputed$test
      }

      # Select genes using inner training participants only
        selected_genes <- select_top_genes(
          X_inner_train,
          n_genes = 500)

        X_inner_train_selected <- as.data.frame(
          X_inner_train[, selected_genes, drop = FALSE])

        X_inner_val_selected <- as.data.frame(
          X_inner_val[, selected_genes, drop = FALSE] )

      # Adding other variables
        if (length(clinical_vars) > 0) {

          X_inner_train_selected <- cbind(
            X_inner_train_selected,
            clinical_inner_train[
              , clinical_vars, drop = FALSE
            ]
          )

          X_inner_val_selected <- cbind(
            X_inner_val_selected,
            clinical_inner_val[
              , clinical_vars, drop = FALSE
            ]
          )
        }

# Fit Random Forest
rf_model <- randomForest(
          x = X_inner_train_selected,
          y = y_inner_train,
          ntree = 500,
          mtry = min(rf_grid[j], ncol(X_inner_train_selected))
        )

# Predict held-out inner participant
        inner_predictions[k] <- predict(
          rf_model,
          newdata = X_inner_val_selected
        )
      }

# Inner LOOCV RMSE
      inner_rmse[j] <- sqrt(
        mean((y_train - inner_predictions)^2)
      )
    }

# Select best mtry
    best_mtry[i] <- rf_grid[which.min(inner_rmse)]

# Select genes using all outer training participants
    selected_genes <- select_top_genes(
      X_train,
      n_genes = 500
    )

    X_train_selected <- as.data.frame(
      X_train[, selected_genes, drop = FALSE]
    )

    X_test_selected <- as.data.frame(
      X_test[, selected_genes, drop = FALSE]
    )

    # dding other variables
    if (length(clinical_vars) > 0) {

      X_train_selected <- cbind(
        X_train_selected,
        clinical_train[, clinical_vars, drop = FALSE]
      )

      X_test_selected <- cbind(
        X_test_selected,
        clinical_test[, clinical_vars, drop = FALSE]
      )
    }

# Fit final outer model
rf_final <- randomForest(
      x = X_train_selected,
      y = y_train,
      ntree = 1000,
      mtry = min(best_mtry[i], ncol(X_train_selected)),
      importance = TRUE
    )

# Predict held-out participant
    predictions[i] <- predict(
      rf_final,
      newdata = X_test_selected
    )

# Baseline prediction
baseline_predictions[i] <- mean(y_train)

# Store variable importance
imp <- importance(rf_final, type = 1)

rf_importance[[i]] <- data.frame(
      variable = rownames(imp),
      importance = as.numeric(imp[, 1])
    )
  }

  return(list(
    predictions = predictions,
    baseline_predictions = baseline_predictions,
    best_mtry = best_mtry,
    importance = rf_importance
  ))
}
```

## Running the three models

Model 1: Genes only
Model 2: Genes + age + sex
Model 3: Genes + age + sex + previous_vax

```{r}
# Model 1: Genes only
rf_model_genes <- run_nested_rf(
  clinical_vars = character(0)
)

# Model 2: Genes + age + sex
rf_model_demo <- run_nested_rf(
  clinical_vars = c("age", "sex")
)

# Model 3: Genes + age + sex + vaccination history
rf_model_full <- run_nested_rf(
  clinical_vars = c(
    "age",
    "sex",
    "vaccination"
  ))
```

## Performance calculation 
```{r}
calculate_metrics <- function(observed, predicted) {

  rmse <- sqrt(mean((observed - predicted)^2))

  r_squared <- 1 -
    sum((observed - predicted)^2) /
    sum((observed - mean(observed))^2)

  c(
    RMSE = rmse,
    R_squared = r_squared
  )
}

# Compare models on log scale
results_log <- rbind(

  Genes_only = calculate_metrics(
    y_log,
    rf_model_genes$predictions
  ),

  Genes_age_sex = calculate_metrics(
    y_log,
    rf_model_demo$predictions
  ),

  Genes_age_sex_vaccination = calculate_metrics(
    y_log,
    rf_model_full$predictions
  ),

  Baseline = calculate_metrics(
    y_log,
    rf_model_genes$baseline_predictions
  )
)

results_log

write.csv(
  results_log,
  here("output", "rf_demo_model_comparison.csv"),
  row.names = TRUE
)
```
The full model is actually performing very slightly better than the baseline, although the difference is extremely small.

However, the negative R² indicates that the model still performs worse than simply predicting the overall mean of the observed outcome.
